clock.asof_source: partition_manifest_v1.json .asof (frozen W1 sealed-calibration clock, reused verbatim)
clock.recent_history_guard_rule: constant-setting receipts read calibration data only through asof - 126 trading days (freeze §4.1 'the W1 calibration clock is honored exactly'; W1's own si_constants_v1.json recent_history_guard reused verbatim as the governing rule text, applied here to the PR-3 constant-setting read rather than re-derived)
clock.recent_history_guard_enforcement: scripts/stock_identity_calibration_replay.py's run_substrate computes recent_history_cutoff(asof) from the combined calendar of the drawn roster's own bars and truncates bars to it BEFORE generating events/episodes, so ep_mod.build_catalog only ever sees through-cutoff bars and censors (never resolves) an episode whose resolution would need later data; a defense-in-depth post-filter then drops any event, and re-censors any episode, that still carries a date beyond the cutoff (a reused W2 fire function can draw on state outside the bars frame it was handed). assert_recent_history_guard is then checked against the substrate's own OUTPUTS (max event signal_known_ts / max episode end_date), never merely against the truncated inputs that fed them, and the cutoff is recorded in provenance_receipt.json. scripts/stock_identity_calibrate_w3.py re-derives the SAME cutoff independently from its own asof/calendar, cross-checks it against the substrate provenance's recorded cutoff (refusing on any mismatch), and re-runs assert_recent_history_guard against the loaded substrate before computing anything -- a second barrier against the substrate's own provenance fields, not against a fresh self-truncated bars copy.
